item.title: Teenage Girl Has Been Missing From the Upper West Side for More Than 6 Weeks: Police
item.dc:creator: Gus Saltonstall
item.description:
Amber Bell was last seen leaving her building on August 12, police said.

The post Teenage Girl Has Been Missing From the Upper West Side for More Than 6 Weeks: Police appeared first on West Side Rag.
item.content:encoded:
By Gus Saltonstall

A teenage girl has been missing from the Upper West Side for more than six weeks, the New York Police Department announced on Tuesday.

Amber Bell, 17, was last seen leaving her apartment building at 216 West 63rd Street at 4 p.m. on August 12, police said.

She was last seen wearing a white tank top, white sneakers, and gray sweatpants, NYPD added.

Bell is five feet, four inches tall, and around 140 pounds, according to police.

Anyone with information regarding this incident is asked to call the NYPD’s Crime Stoppers Hotline at 1-800-577-TIPS (8477) or for Spanish, 1-888-57-PISTA (74782).

item.title: Big Tree Falls on Central Park West
item.dc:creator: Gus Saltonstall
item.description:
The tree on Central Park West, between West 94th and 95th streets, showed clear signs of instability in the lead up to its fall.

The post Big Tree Falls on Central Park West appeared first on West Side Rag.
item.content:encoded:
By Gus Saltonstall

A large tree crashed to the earth on the Upper West Side sometime late Tuesday or early Wednesday.

The tree fell backward on Central Park West, between West 94th and 95th streets, over the barrier to the park. Prior to its fall, the tree had been stationed on the sidewalk of Central Park West.

The force of the tree ripping out of its roots damaged the surrounding cobblestones and pavement.

Multiple people stopped to gawk and photograph the fallen tree on Wednesday morning. One teenager ducked the yellow tape and attempted to jump and touch the top of the stump after a debate over whether it was taller than a basketball hoop.

He didn’t reach it.

Google Maps imagery from August 2026 shows the tree had clearly been leaning backward.

Multiple “tree care” trucks cleaned up the scene Wednesday morning. The teams were cutting up the tree from its top side and loading the wooden carcass into vehicles.

Thanks to Mark Maas for tipping us off about the downed tree.

item.title: Elevators at Major Upper West Side Train Station Reopen
item.dc:creator: Gus Saltonstall
item.description:
The elevators are back up and running at the West 72nd Street 1, 2, and 3 train station.

The post Elevators at Major Upper West Side Train Station Reopen appeared first on West Side Rag.
item.content:encoded:
By Gus Saltonstall

The elevators at a major Upper West Side train station reopened this week.

The two elevators at the West 72nd Street and Broadway 1, 2, and 3 train station are back up and running after more than a year of repair work.

The Rag witnessed multiple people ride the elevators Wednesday morning, and a Metropolitan Transportation Authority worker standing nearby confirmed they were back in service.

The 72nd Street elevators had been closed for replacement work since August 2025. The repairs were connected to “better reliability,” adding “modernized equipment,” creating a “smoother ride,” and “upgrading the security systems,” the MTA said at the time.

Initially, the MTA said the elevators would reopen by March of 2026, which was then pushed back to the summer of 2026, with the work actually concluding at the end of September 2026.

A 90-foot construction staging area was erected outside the West 72nd Street station within Verdi Square for the elevator work, which is still up as of Wednesday morning.

With the elevators back up and running, the staging equipment should come down in the near future.

item.title: Openings & Closings: TALEA Beer Co.; Velvet Cowboy; Kine Musubi; Topman Barbershop; Cafe des Artistes; 7th Street Burger
item.dc:creator: Lisa Kava
item.description:
A female-founded brewery and a Hawaiian comfort-food restaurant are among the newest businesses to open on the UWS.

The post Openings & Closings: TALEA Beer Co.; Velvet Cowboy; Kine Musubi; Topman Barbershop; Cafe des Artistes; 7th Street Burger appeared first on West Side Rag.
item.content:encoded:
By Lisa Kava and Julia Ornedo

TALEA  Beer Co., a female-founded brewery, opened on September 25th at 441 Amsterdam Avenue (between West 81st and 82nd streets). TALEA was founded in 2019 by Tara Hankinson and LeAnn Darland with a mission to expand craft beer “beyond the beer bros,” Hankinson wrote to West Side Rag in an email. The duo sold beer door to door, eventually opening a location in Williamsburg, Brooklyn. They have since opened five other locations in NYC. TALEA brews a variety of beer styles including bestseller Al Dente, an Italian-style Pilsner, and specialty sour beers like Pina Colada Splash and Rainbow Cookie. The Upper West Side location features an all-day menu with “heartier dishes for evenings and weekends,” Hankinson wrote. “Our menu will include brunchy and lunch crowd favorites, entrees for evenings and kid friendly food.” Hankinson and Darland are both moms of young children and wanted to create a space that could work for a date night and for a Sunday morning with the kids, she said. St. James Gate, the Irish pub which closed in 2024, was the last tenant in the space. (Thanks to Ben for the tip.)

Velvet Cowboy, a Western bar, opened on September 29th at  509 Amsterdam Avenue (between West 84th and 85th streets). It is in the space previously occupied by Jacob’s Pickles, which moved in October 2025, and is under the same ownership. Velvet Cowboy features a $5 food menu which includes Texas chili, frito pie and a take on a McRib according to The Infatuation. Reservations for the cocktail lounge are available starting October 1st on Resy, which describes Velvet Cowboy as “inspired by the untamed spirit of the American Southwest.”

Kine Musubi, a Hawaiian musubi restaurant, had a soft opening at 128 West 72nd Street on September 24th.  Musubi is a popular snack food in Hawaii, similar to sushi. It is made with  rice topped with Spam or other savory ingredients and topped with seaweed. The restaurant’s co-founder Chi Ian Chan, grew up in Hawaii and moved to NYC in 2022. He previously had a pop up inside of the restaurant Sushi Nonaka which closed in April 2025. Kine Musubi does not yet have set hours, as the staff is still in training, a representative told West Side Rag via social media. A smoke shop was previously in the space. (Thanks to Myra for the tip.)

Topman Barbershop, a barbershop, opened at 2592 Broadway (between West 97th and 98th streets), on August 22nd. This is the third location for the barbershop and the second on the Upper West Side. Topman opened on West 79th Street (at Amsterdam Avenue), in 2024. Services include men’s haircuts, buzzcuts, shaves, and waxing. Mono Cleaners, a dry cleaner, was previously in the space. (Thanks to Elliot and Karen for the tip.)

ICYMI:

Café des Artistes, the iconic long- time Upper West Side restaurant, which closed in 2009, has announced it will reopen, “returning to its original glamour,” at 1 West 67th Street (between Central Park West and Columbus Avenue), in early 2027. In honor of the reopening, they are asking former diners, staff, and neighbors of Café des Artistes to send memories of the space to memories@cafedesartistesnyc.com. Read West Side Rag’s coverage of this news here.

7th Street Burger, a casual burger place, at 424 Amsterdam Avenue (between West 80th and 81st streets), is temporarily closed due to a gas issue. Read West Side Rag’s coverage of this news here.

The Openings & Closings column wouldn’t be possible without our many tipsters: thank you! Anyone can send tips about openings and closings in the neighborhood to info@westsiderag.com.

item.title: 4 Upper West Side Private Schools Named Among 100 Best in New York City
item.dc:creator: Gus Saltonstall
item.description:
The Collegiate School took home the honor as the top ranked private high school on the Upper West Side.

The post 4 Upper West Side Private Schools Named Among 100 Best in New York City appeared first on West Side Rag.
item.content:encoded:
By Gus Saltonstall

A total of four Upper West Side private high schools made a recent ranking of the 100 best in New York City.

On Monday, Niche released its annual rankings of the best schools in the United States, where it analyzed 93,000 public schools and 30,000 private schools across the country.

Four Upper West Side schools landed spots in Niche’s ranking of New York City’s 100 best private schools for 2027.

The top-ranked New York City private high school in the neighborhood? The Collegiate School.

  • #14: The Collegiate School at 301 Freedom Place South (between West 61st and 62nd streets)
  • #20: Trinity School at 139 West 91st Street (between Amsterdam and Columbus)
  • #31: Columbia Grammar & Preparatory School at 5 West 93rd Street (between Columbus and Central Park West)
  • #72: The Calhoun School at 433 West End Avenue (between West 80th and 81st streets)

Niche’s rankings combine federal and state data, school statistics, and over 3 million reviews from students, parents, and teachers, to evaluate schools. You can read more about Niche’s methodology in the seven-step breakdown of its process — HERE.

It is the first time since at least 2018 that no Upper West Side private school earned a spot in Niche’s top 10 for New York City.

West Side Rag did note some discrepancies in Niche’s filtering system, as schools outside of the five boroughs were grouped into New York City.

For example, Rye Country Day School in Rye, New York, continued to appear as the fifth-best private high school in New York City. The Rag changed the rankings accordingly to not include schools outside of the city.

Most eye-catching is Trinity’s ranking as the 20th best private high school in New York City.

Niche named Trinity as the best private school in New York City for three years in a row from 2019 to 2022, and among the 25 best in the United States from 2019 through 2023.

Here are the grades Niche gave Trinity for the 2027 school year:

  • Academics: A+
  • Teachers: A
  • Clubs & Activities: B
  • Diversity: A
  • College Prep: A+
  • Sports: C+

Here are the yearly tuition costs at the four top Upper West Side private high schools when paid at full price, according to their websites. All four of the schools provide financial aid at various levels for students.

  • Collegiate School: $72,070
  • Trinity School: $71,500
  • Columbia Grammar & Preparatory School: $69,560
  • The Calhoun School: $69,500

Here are the top 10 private high schools in New York City for 2027, according to Niche.

  1. The Chapin School
  2. Horace Mann School
  3. BASIS Independent Manhattan
  4. Riverdale Country School
  5. BASIS Independent Brooklyn
  6. The Spence School
  7. Regis High School
  8. Avenue The World School
  9. Nightingdale-Bamford School
  10. Dalton

You can check out the full rankings from Niche — HERE.

item.title: As the Weekend Storm Departs, A Look Back at the Spectacular UWS Sunsets it Produced
item.dc:creator: Gus Saltonstall
item.description:
"There were two evenings of spectacular sunset to enjoy," UWSer Joe Josephs said.

The post As the Weekend Storm Departs, A Look Back at the Spectacular UWS Sunsets it Produced appeared first on West Side Rag.
item.content:encoded:
By Gus Saltonstall

As this weekend’s nor’easter storm made its final push in New York City on Monday, here are a few more photos of the spectacular sunsets that danced across the Upper West Side skies over the last few days.

Central Park recorded 2.57 inches of rain from Friday through Sunday. The worst flooding in the five boroughs took place outside of Manhattan in Hamilton Beach, Howard Beach and Broad Channel in Queens.

A tree did come down on West 94th Street, though.

Here is how Upper West Sider Joe Josephs described capturing the skies over the neighborhood.

“Before the nor’easter darkened our skies there were two evenings of spectacular sunset to enjoy and in my case photograph,” Josephs wrote. “All the photos attached were taken on 9/24 and 9/25 from the deck of my UWS apartment [on West End Avenue in the 90s].”

item.title: Ruthless Advice for Upper West Siders: All of the Answers With None of the Expertise
item.dc:creator: Laura Muha
item.description:
I shut the bathroom door and said to my wife, “There’s a rat on the toilet.”

The post Ruthless Advice for Upper West Siders: All of the Answers With None of the Expertise appeared first on West Side Rag.
item.content:encoded:
By Cynthia Kaplan and Otis, a Welsh terrier

Fall is officially here. To kick it off, your Ruthless advisor sent Otis to a friend’s house and went off for a week of hiking in the national parks of Utah. Breathtaking, both visually and physiologically. Who knew there were so many humongous rock formations? Centuries of the earth pushing itself up in different ways, creating cool/frightening monoliths of all shapes and sizes, which in turn were eroded by water and wind, revealing canyons and peaks and arches. There were sky-high towers that looked like rocks piled on top of each other but were actually single formations called hoo doos, which to the trained eye all looked like either Bart Simpson or penises. And almost everywhere there were also small caves and holes carved into the rock walls which were made by women from the pioneer era to the current day trying to claw their way out of the valleys so as not be married off to men in their 80s when they were 10 years old. Just a hypothesis.

Dear Ruthless,

We had dinner with a client of my husband’s and his wife, whom neither of us had ever met. When we arrived at the restaurant, we were all introduced. The wife, a beautiful woman, I would guess around 40, was wearing a decorative turban, the kind often worn by women going through chemo. When she was ordering she lightly mentioned her taste buds were off, and I asked her if she was in treatment. She then told us, yes, that her diagnosis was recent, over the evening we talked quite a bit about her experience. Later, my husband told me he thought I’d been nosy and intrusive, but I think the wife noticeably relaxed when she realized she didn’t have to hide to make us comfortable. Was I wrong?

Signed,

Not Nosy Nellie

Dear Not,

CINDY: It is my own lived experience that pretending not to notice someone’s reality, from a cancer diagnosis to a painful loss, is like pretending they don’t exist as a human. We all suffer, and having it acknowledged, even by a stranger, is often appreciated. It sounds like she proffered a subtle invitation to hold space for her and you accepted. People will let you know quickly how personal they want to get, and abiding by the boundaries they set is important. I think the key is listening well. Let the person suffering lead. Don’t share your own ills unless asked. Don’t say you know how they feel unless you actually have their exact problem. And don’t be that person who digs a little too excitedly into other people’s troubles. NO ONE LIKES THAT.

OTIS: You sound like a thoughtful, empathetic person, and I think your husband was clearly not paying attention to how your kind interest was received. I think perhaps he was expressing his own discomfort. That said, I’d like a little more information. What were you all eating? Did anyone have chicken or cheese or both?

Dear Ruthless,

In the wake of the latest Trader Joe’s escalator horror, should the city (or state, or country) consider an age limit on who can use an escalator? I feel terrible for the poor woman at the bottom of the pile who was so badly injured and to add insult to injury, had to miss her daughter’s wedding.

Signed,

Concerned Shopper

Dear Concerned,

OTIS: Cindy and I are deeply upset by the accident, and our thoughts are with those involved, but accidents are caused by people of all ages. If you are nervous, which is understandable, shop somewhere else for now. If you want legislation, consider going after those people who ignore leash laws because they think their dog is better than everyone else’s dog. They’re not.

CINDY: Yes, Otis and I indeed are sending healing thoughts to the victim of the escalator accident. To the question: No one likes an escalator, especially since You-Know-Which old man rode down one announcing his candidacy/the end of democracy. Maybe if we’d had a law in place in 2016, this nachtmare could have been avoided. Write to your congressperson. Start the process. See how far it goes.

Dear Ruthless,

Let me set the scene. During this latest deluge, I returned home from a dinner with a friend, soaked to the skin, and after a cup of hot tea, happily climbed into my warm, dry bed, next to my warm, dry wife. I dozed briefly, waking to remember I hadn’t taken a pill I was supposed to take. I got up, went to the bathroom, opened the door, and in the soft light leaking from the nearby street lamp, I saw, perched on the seat of the toilet, a rat. A rat! I shut the door and said to my wife, “There’s a rat on the toilet.” I got up, and as we opened the door, we heard a splash. It was gone, leaving the seat wet. We complained to the building superintendent, who first tried to gaslight us, claiming it couldn’t have happened, and then asked us to not tell our neighbors. Wouldn’t you tell your neighbors?

Signed,

Rats on Four

Dear Rats,

CINDY: Oof, sorry. I’m not sure I’d ever use that bathroom again. This is a building issue. I would write to the board, demanding steps be taken. If they respond quickly and effectively, I’d hold off on the mass (hysteria) email. I would, however, dine out on the story every chance I got, and if some of those dinner partners are neighbors, so be it.

OTIS: I’ve just started a business trapping toilet-hopping rats. It’s a little expensive, but you get what you pay for.

Dear Ruthless,

When I host our family and friends for dinner on holidays, I use place cards. I like to mix and match couples and kids so everyone has the opportunity for new conversations and relationships. My mother-in-law consistently changes the seating to suit herself! I don’t want to fight with her in public and I’ve had the discussion in private before. Oy!

Signed,

It’s My Party

Dear It’s,

OTIS: I don’t sit where I’m told, either.

CINDY: It IS your party. Explain to your mother-in-law that you love having her over, but the next time she rearranges your placecards, you will take hers and rip it up in front of the crowd, then call her a cab.

Cynthia Kaplan is the co-creator, with Karen Bergreen, of this column and of The Ruthless Comedy Hour, a comedy variety show for grownups with brains. In its 12 years, the Comedy Hour featured top stand-up comedians musicians and celebrity interviews, and addressed social, political, and local concerns by making brutal fun of them. Bergreen is a veteran stand-up comedian and author of two acclaimed novels. Kaplan tours extensively with her comedy rock band, The Cynthia Kaplan Ordeal, and is the author of two just as acclaimed collections of humorous essays.

Otis is a 12-year-old Welsh terrier. He is a life-long Upper West Sider. In his neighborhood he is known by many and loved by few. 

Got a question in need of ruthless advice? Email Ruthless at info@westsiderag.com.

item.title: Popular UWS 7th Street Burger Temporarily Closed Due to Gas Issue in its Building
item.dc:creator: Gus Saltonstall
item.description:
7th Street Burger on the Upper West Side has been closed since Saturday.

The post Popular UWS 7th Street Burger Temporarily Closed Due to Gas Issue in its Building appeared first on West Side Rag.
item.content:encoded:
UPDATE: Monday, September 28 at 6 p.m.: The popular 7th Street Burger Upper West Side location is temporarily closed due to a gas issue in the building, Sarah Milner, a marketing manager for 7th Street Burger, told West Side Rag in an email on Monday evening.

The outpost at 424 Amsterdam Avenue, between West 80th and 81st streets, has been shuttered since Saturday.

“We should be back open this week! There was a gas issue in the building, so we were required to close while the issue was investigated,” Milner told the Rag. “It has since been resolved and we are awaiting final approval to open!”

Original Story

By Gus Saltonstall

The popular 7th Street Burger outpost at 424 Amsterdam Avenue, between West 80th and 81st streets, is temporarily closed.

The reason for the closure remains unclear.

The fast-casual burger spot has been shuttered since at least Saturday.

“Any idea why 7th St Burger on Amsterdam Ave is currently closed?” an Upper West Sider, who wished to remain anonymous, wrote to West Side Rag in an email on Saturday at 2:15 p.m.

As of Monday at 2:30 p.m., Google lists the Upper West Side eatery as “Temporarily closed.”

The Rag visited the 7th Street Burger location around 11 a.m. on Monday and found its silver metal gate completely down. However, we returned around 2 p.m. to find the gate up, but the business still shuttered.

After knocking, a man unlocked the front door and then directed the Rag to ask our question to a different person near the back of the burger joint.

“Why are you closed?” the Rag asked.

“It’s all good; we’re just closed for a few more days,” responded the man, who did not provide his name.

“Can you tell me why you’re closed?”

“No, not right now,” the man said.

There was no yellow Health Department closure sign on the 7th Street Burger’s front door and the city’s Health Department portal says it received an “A” in its most recent inspection in March of 2026.

7th Street Burger has more than 10 locations across New York City and is popular for its smash burger and late-night hours. The hamburger chain did not immediately respond to the Rag’s request for comment.

We will update this story if we learn more.

item.title: Pedestrian Dies 4 Days After Being Struck by Cyclist in Central Park: ‘Our Hearts are Broken’
item.dc:creator: Gus Saltonstall
item.description:
Richie O'Brien is survived by his wife and two young daughters.

The post Pedestrian Dies 4 Days After Being Struck by Cyclist in Central Park: ‘Our Hearts are Broken’ appeared first on West Side Rag.
item.content:encoded:
By Gus Saltonstall

A pedestrian struck by a cyclist in Central Park last week succumbed to his injuries on Sunday, the man’s family announced.

Richie O’Brien, 41, was walking to his job as a union steamfitter around 6:35 a.m. on Wednesday, September 23, when he was struck by a 32-year-old cyclist on a pedal bike, police said.

An NYPD spokesperson told West Side Rag that the collision happened near the Metropolitan Museum of Art within the park on East Drive at 84th Street.

“The bicyclist struck the pedestrian causing him to fall to the ground sustaining severe head trauma,” police told West Side Rag in an email.

O’Brien was rushed to Weill-Cornell hospital in critical condition with severe head trauma, and placed in a medically induced coma.

The bicyclist remained on the scene with minor injuries, police told WSR. There have been no arrests, according to NYPD.

O’Brien died on Sunday morning, his family announced online.

“Richie passed away peacefully in the early morning hours of Sunday, September 27,  with Ronni [his wife] by his side,” the note read. “Although our hearts are broken by this unimaginable loss, Richie’s legacy will live on. He was able to give the gift of life to others through organ donation, helping those in need even in his final moments.”

O’Brien is survived by his wife Ronni and their eight- and 12-year-old daughters.

“Ronni has been a devoted stay-at-home mom, dedicating herself to raising their two daughters, Kylie and Mia, who are just 8 and 12 years old,” reads a note connected to a fundraiser for the family. “Now, while caring for her children and remaining by Richie’s side through this unimaginable time, she is also facing the uncertainty of having to support her family without Richie’s income.”

The investigation remains ongoing by the NYPD Highway District’s Collision Investigation Squad.
